text:
Pittsburgh played the better game and lost it. The Penguins generated 3.52 expected goals to Chicago's 3.46 and took 61 shot attempts to 34, enough that the simulations give PIT a 76 percent chance to win a replay. The difference was in the net. Sergei Murashov allowed 2.0 goals more than the shots against him deserved, while Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27.

Chicago scored early and kept finding the cheap ones. Teuvo Teravainen opened the game 28 seconds in, and Roman Kantserov added a power-play goal late in the first and another at 10:32 of the second for a 3-1 lead. PIT answered with its best stretch in the second, out-chancing CHI 1.96 to 0.74 in expected goals, but Nick Robertson's goal at 17:51 was the only payoff. Rickard Rakell had a 19 percent look in that period that Knight turned away. Sidney Crosby tied it at 3-3 in the third, his second of the night.

Then came the game's strangest goal. Teravainen scored at 15:42 on a wrist shot worth just a 1 percent chance, and CHI led 4-3. Tyler Bertuzzi sealed it at 19:50 with a tip-in for the 5-3 final, the only one of the late goals that looked like a real chance (88 percent). Teravainen finished with two goals and an assist, Kantserov had two goals, and Connor Bedard added an assist. PIT went 0 for 4 on the power play, while CHI scored on one of its two.
